headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors: Devin can ingest Perplexity outputs and act on them with write/network privileges.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can read files, use MCP, and browse; Perplexity produces web-derived content and citations. That creates a plausible path where Devin ingests Perplexity output as trusted instructions. The bridge is not a shared filesystem by default, so this is below high, but still present in documented pairings.
conditions: IF Devin consumes Perplexity output without provenance filtering
IF Perplexity returns attacker-controlled text that Devin treats as instructions
mitigations: Require explicit provenance labels on Perplexity outputs
Strip imperative text before passing results to Devin
Use a human review step for any copied instructions
Disable direct copy-paste of raw search summaries
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs, while Perplexity handles uploaded documents and browsing context. If the same sensitive material is shared into both, Perplexity’s vendor-hosted backend can expose it beyond the original workspace. The profiles do not prove a default shared filesystem, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF the same confidential document is uploaded to Perplexity after Devin accessed it
IF Devin forwards repo secrets or internal chat into Perplexity prompts
mitigations: Do not upload secrets or internal chat to Perplexity
Redact sensitive fields before sharing outputs
Use separate workspaces for confidential and public tasks
Review Perplexity privacy settings before use
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on cross-agent handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can write files, modify git state, and use broad network egress; Perplexity cannot write the filesystem or modify git state and is vendor-only for egress. Overlapping write conflict is therefore limited, with the main risk being coordination mistakes rather than direct concurrent mutation of the same resources.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repo clone or workspace
IF Devin commits while Perplexity is only reading and summarizing
mitigations: Assign Devin sole write ownership of the repo
Keep Perplexity read-only for shared artifacts
Pause Devin before copying Perplexity suggestions into git
Use branch protection and PR review
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor with shell, browser, and write privileges, while Perplexity performs multi-hop browsing and returns cited answers. If Devin treats Perplexity’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes, commits, or external actions. The pair’s default interaction is therefore dangerous and can cause irreversible downstream mistakes.
conditions: IF Devin uses Perplexity answers as facts without verification
IF Devin applies Perplexity-derived instructions to code or tickets
mitigations: Require source verification before Devin acts
Have Devin cross-check critical claims against primary sources
Limit Perplexity to research-only tasks
Review any generated plan before execution
requires-engineering: add confidence gating on handoff

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens and touches team chat/docs, while Perplexity processes uploaded documents and browsing context under vendor-hosted infrastructure. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch for sensitive internal data and retention expectations. The profiles do not show a specific residency regime, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF regulated or confidential data is sent from Devin into Perplexity
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two services
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity
Use a data-classification checklist before handoff
Confirm vendor retention settings for both tools
Separate public and confidential workflows
requires-engineering: document a compliance-approved data flow
